---
title: "Configuration reference"
---

Two places hold configuration: a document's **YAML front matter** (the `---`
block at the top), and a project's **`_site.yml`** (for a site or book). The
project config uses a flat, native schema. A Quarto-shaped nested config (a
`project:` / `website:` / `book:` / `format:` block) is no longer parsed: its
unknown top-level keys warn, and its nested values are ignored. Flatten it (see
the note at the end).

## Document front matter

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title`, `subtitle`, `author`, `date`, `description` | Metadata; `title` drives `<title>`, the title block, OpenGraph, and nav/listing labels |
| `format` | `html` (default) or `revealjs`; or `<ext>-html` / `<ext>-revealjs` to load a format extension |
| `theme` | `light` (default) / `dark`, a `.css`/`.scss` file, or an installed `_extensions/<name>/` |
| `toc` | `true` adds a live table of contents (+ the Cmd-K search palette) |
| `title-block-style` | `none` keeps the title metadata but hides the visible `<h1>` header |
| `bibliography` | A `.bib` file enabling `[@key]` citations + an auto References section (rendered in a single built-in IEEE style) |
| `page-layout` | `full` widens the content column (for listing indexes) |
| `include-in-header` / `include-before-body` / `include-after-body` | Inject raw markup; each is a path, a `{ text: … }` / `{ file: … }` map, or a list of those |
| `css` | Stylesheet(s) wrapped in `<style>` and inlined |
| `lang` | BCP-47 language tag for `<html lang>` (default `en`) |
| `csl` | Recognized so it never warns, but **not currently honored**: references always render in the built-in IEEE style, so setting `csl` has no effect |
| `categories`, `image`, `image-alt` | `categories`/`image` feed `listing:` cards + social meta; `image-alt` sets the alt text on an `about:` profile image (listing-card images emit an empty `alt`) |
| `extensions` | A list of `_extensions/<name>/` to load (shortcodes, format theming) |
| `draft` | `true` excludes the page from a website build (output, nav, and listings) |

### Code-cell options

Inside a cell, lines beginning `#|` (`//|` for `{js}`, `%%|` for `{mermaid}`)
set per-cell options:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `echo: false` | Hide the source, show only the output |
| `code-fold: true` + `code-summary: "…"` | Collapse the listing behind a summary |
| `label: fig-… ` + `fig-cap: "…"` | Make the output a numbered, cross-referenceable figure |
| `include: false` | Run the cell but drop its output |

A front-matter `execute:` block sets document-wide `echo`/`include`/`cache` defaults
that a cell's own `#|` options override.

## Project `_site.yml`

A **directory** with a `_site.yml` is a site or book project. The schema is
flat: qmd-fast is HTML-only, so there's no `format: html:` nesting, and the
project type is inferred (presence of `chapters:` ⇒ a book). There is no
`_metadata.yml` cascade: the root config sets defaults, a page's own front matter
overrides them.

A **website**:

```yaml
title: "My Site"
description: "Notes on things"
url: "https://example.com"
favicon: favicon.svg
output: _site            # build output dir (default _site, or _book for a book)
toc: true                # default table of contents for article pages
css: custom.css
head: head.html          # = include-in-header  (also: body-start, body-end)

nav:                     # a list is the left side; or { left: [...], right: [...] }
  - { text: Blog,     href: blog.qmd }
  - { text: Projects, href: projects.qmd }

footer:                  # a string is left text; or { left, center, right }
  left: "© 2026 Me"
  right:
    - { icon: github, href: "https://github.com/me" }
```

A **book**: just add `chapters:` (its presence makes it a book; no `type:`):

```yaml
title: "My Book"
author: "Me"
toc: true
chapters:
  - index.qmd
  - part: "Part One"     # group chapters under a part header
    chapters: [a.qmd, b.qmd]
  - file: c.qmd          # { file:, text: } overrides the sidebar label
    text: "Conclusions"
```

A chapter entry is a bare path (`- a.qmd`), a `{ part:, chapters: }` group header, or
a `{ file:, text: }` mapping whose `text:` overrides the sidebar label (the override
also works inside a part's list). Without `text:`, the label is the chapter's first
`# H1`, then its front-matter `title:`, then the file stem.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title`, `author`, `description`, `url` | Project metadata (`title` is the navbar brand / book title) |
| `favicon` | Tab icon (defaults to the qmd-fast mark) |
| `image` | Default social-card image for pages that don't set their own |
| `output` | Build output directory |
| `toc` | Default table of contents for article pages |
| `css`, `head`, `body-start`, `body-end` | Site-wide asset injection (a path, `{ text: … }` / `{ file: … }`, or a list) |
| `nav` | Navbar items: a list (left), or `{ left, right }` |
| `footer` | Footer: a string, or `{ left, center, right }` of items |
| `chapters` | Book chapter order (a file, `{ file, text }`, or `{ part, chapters }`); presence ⇒ a book |
| `mounts` | Mount other qmd-fast projects under a URL prefix in **preview**: a map `{ docs: ../docs }` or a list of `{ at, path }`. The static build skips mounts and prints the per-mount build command |

**Icons.** A nav/footer item can be `{ icon: <name>, href: … }` instead of raw
HTML; bundled glyphs: `github`, `linkedin`, `rss`, `x`, `mastodon`, `bluesky`,
`email`.

**Validation.** Unrecognized keys are reported with a "did you mean …" hint, offered
when a known key is within edit distance 2, so a typo like `favicn:` doesn't silently do
nothing. Validation only **warns**: the document still renders, and every warning is
**located**, so in the live preview you can click it straight to the source line. The same
closed-vocabulary check covers unknown cell `#|` options and unknown immediate children of
`execute:` / `listing:` / `about:` / `hero:`; `format:` sub-keys are intentionally left
unlinted, since a format extension may add its own. (The Internals book covers the design,
and the drift-locked Draft 2020-12 schemas behind the `qmd-fast schema` command, in its
*Validation & schemas* chapter.)

## Editor autocomplete (config schema)

qmd-fast ships JSON Schemas for both config surfaces so your editor's YAML
language server can autocomplete keys, show hovers, and flag unknown keys as you
type, before you render. There is no qmd-fast language server to install: the
schemas describe the same key sets qmd-fast validates against at render time, so
the editor and the renderer always agree.

Drop the schemas into your project:

```sh
qmd-fast schema --out .qmd
```

Then point the YAML language server at them with a modeline.

For `_site.yml` (a plain YAML file, works out of the box), add at the very top:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=.qmd/qmd-site.schema.json
title: My site
```

For a document's front matter, put the modeline inside the `---` block:

```yaml
---
# yaml-language-server: $schema=.qmd/qmd-frontmatter.schema.json
title: My post
---
```

Front-matter validation needs an editor that treats a `.qmd` file's `---` block
as embedded YAML (for example the VS Code YAML extension). A plain YAML language
server does not parse a `.qmd` file as YAML, so the front-matter modeline only
takes effect with that support; `_site.yml` needs no such setup.

::: {.callout-note}
## Quarto migration

The nested Quarto shape is no longer parsed, so flatten it: lift
`website: title:` to `title:`, `format: html: toc:` to `toc:`,
`website: navbar: left:` to `nav:`, `page-footer:` to `footer:`, and
`project: output-dir:` to `output:`. Any leftover nested top-level key
(`project:`, `website:`, `book:`) will warn as unknown.
:::

### Page blocks (sites)

Two front-matter blocks turn a page into something special:

```yaml
# an index page: a card per document under `contents:`
listing:
  contents: posts          # directory to crawl
  type: grid               # grid | (default) stacked list
  sort: "date desc"
  max-items: 10
  categories: true         # render a category filter row
  id: recent               # optional: fill a `::: {#recent}` block instead of appending

# a profile page (the homepage)
about:
  template: jolla
  image: me.jpg
  links: [{ text: "GitHub", href: "https://github.com/…" }]
```

## Project structure & reserved names

A multi-page project is just a directory with a `_site.yml`. qmd-fast discovers the
pages by walking that directory, with one rule: **anything whose name starts with
`_` or `.` is not a page.** That single convention is what keeps config, partials,
caches, and build output from turning into navigable pages.

```text
my-site/
├── _site.yml            # project config; presence makes this a site/book
├── index.qmd            # a page (the home page)
├── about.qmd            # a page
├── posts/
│   └── first.qmd        # a page (nested pages are discovered too)
├── _includes/           # `_`-prefixed ⇒ skipped: partials for {{< include >}}
│   └── _disclaimer.qmd
├── _extensions/         # `_`-prefixed ⇒ skipped: format extensions
│   └── my-theme/
├── _freeze/             # `_`-prefixed ⇒ skipped: execution cache (gitignored)
└── _site/               # build output (_book/ for a book; override with output:)
```

Reserved names, all skipped by page discovery:

| Name | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `_site.yml` | the project config (its presence is what defines a project) |
| `_includes/` | a convention for `{{< include >}}` partials; the `_` keeps them out of the page set (the leading `_` on the partial files themselves, e.g. `_intro.qmd`, is also enough) |
| `_extensions/` | format extensions (custom `format:`s, shortcodes) |
| `_freeze/` | the persistent execution cache, keyed by content hash; gitignore it |
| `_site/` / `_book/` | build output (`build <dir>` writes here; override with `output:`) |
| anything `.`-prefixed | hidden files/dirs (`.git`, `.quarto`, …) are skipped too |

A `404.qmd` is special-cased the other way: it builds to `404.html` at the site root
(most static hosts serve it for unknown URLs) but stays out of the nav.

### How a deck gets built

A slide deck is any doc with `format: revealjs`. How it ends up in your output
depends on *how the project refers to it*: there are three cases, and missing the
distinction is the usual way a deck goes missing from a build:

- **Standalone**: `qmd-fast preview deck.qmd` or `qmd-fast build deck.qmd`. The deck
  is the whole document; it renders as slides. Nothing else needed.
- **Embedded**: `{{< embed deck.qmd >}}` from a page or chapter. The deck is built as
  its own standalone slide file and shown inline as an isolating iframe; it is kept
  *out* of the nav and search (it isn't a page, it's an inclusion). This is how to put
  a deck inside a site or book. See [Formats](../using/formats.qmd).
- **Loose (warns)**: a `format: revealjs` file sitting in a site directory that no
  page embeds and that isn't a standalone target. It is neither chaptered nor embedded,
  so the build has no reason to emit it; qmd-fast warns and would otherwise flatten it
  into a chrome-wrapped article. **Fix:** embed it from a page, or build it standalone.
